## Stage counts (all add up)
| Stage | Count |
|---|---|
| Non-blank order rows | 1842 (7 blank lines skipped, not counted as rows) |
| Malformed | 41 |
| Valid | 1801 (1842 − 41) |
| Distinct order ids | 1445, so 1801 − 1445 = **356** duplicates removed |
| Cancelled | 191 |
| Test | 362 |
| Included | 892 (1445 − 191 − 362) |
| Refund rows | 159: 5 repeated ids, 123 matched, 31 ignored (unknown, cancelled or test orders) |

Gross is $117,375.98 and refunds are $9,616.98, which gives a refund rate of 0.0819.

The offset handling matters in this data. In 69 orders with several versions, comparing `updated_at` as plain text would have picked a different winner than comparing actual times. Four valid versions have an `updated_at` in 2026. They are compared normally.

## Interpretation decisions and rows affected
- **Strict whitespace:** stripping and case-folding only for currency, status, `is_test` and the `test-` prefix. **0** rows were rejected only because of this; no other field has stray spaces.
- **Email domain:** the text after the last `@` must equal `test.shopco.io`, ignoring case. The 4 rows at `latest.shopco.io` stay real customers.
- **Ties:** if two versions have the same `updated_at` time, the one read last wins. There were **0** ties.
- **Bad refund rows:** rows with an unparseable amount or unknown currency are skipped and not counted as malformed. There were **0** in this export.
- **Repeated refund ids:** the first occurrence is kept. **5** repeats were dropped.
- **No capping:** refunds are not capped at the order's gross value, so an order's net revenue can go negative. Fully refunded orders don't make their customer a paying customer, using the README's cents test.
- **Quarter keys:** `2025-Q1` to `2025-Q4` are always present. Any other year would get its own key, but no included order is dated outside 2025, so none were added.
- **Top product ties:** the alphabetically first product would win. This didn't come up.

## Data the README didn't cover
- **Other bad values:** besides the listed traps there are a `unit_price` of `12,99x` and a blank one, a currency of `EURO`, quantity `n/a`, `order_date` values `n/a` and `yesterday`, and `updated_at` values `soon` and blank. All count as malformed.
- **Short rows:** some rows have 11 fields, which is also a field-count mismatch, so they count as malformed.
- **Rows with every field empty:** treated as blank lines, so they are skipped and not counted (7 of them).
- **Refunds:** 6 refunds point at ids that appear in none of the order files, and they are ignored. 6 refunds are dated in 2026 and still count against their order.
